chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Faḍḍāl and Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, all of them said: We presented the Book of Inheritances from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, and he said:

And among what it contained was: “Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام fixed the diyah of the fetus at one hundred dinars, and he made the semen of the man, until it becomes a fetus, into five parts. So when it is a fetus before the spirit enters into it, it is one hundred dinars. That is because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the human being from an extract, and that is the drop of fluid; this is one part. Then a clot, so that is two parts. Then a lump of flesh, three parts. Then bone, so that is four parts. Then it is clothed with flesh; at that point it has become a complete fetus, and its five parts are complete: one hundred dinars. And the one hundred dinars are five parts, so he assigned to the drop one-fifth of the hundred, twenty dinars; to the clot, two-fifths of the hundred, forty dinars; to the lump of flesh, three-fifths of the hundred, sixty dinars; and to the bone, four-fifths of the hundred, eighty dinars. Then when another creation is produced in it, namely the spirit, then at that point it is a soul: one thousand full dinars if it is male, and if it is female then five hundred dinars.

And if a woman is killed while pregnant, and the pregnancy had become complete but she did not cast out her child, and it is not known whether it was male or female, and it is not known whether it died after her or before her, then its diyah is two halves: half the diyah of a male and half the diyah of a female. And the diyah of the woman is complete after that, and that is six parts in relation to the fetus.

And he عليه السلام gave the ruling regarding the semen of a man who is startled away from his bride, so he withholds the fluid from her without intending that: half of one-fifth of the hundred, ten dinars; and if he discharges in her, then twenty dinars.

And he ruled regarding the diyah for injuries to the fetus from the basis of the hundred, according to what applies in the injuries of the male and female, the man and the woman, in full. And he assigned for it retaliation concerning its injury and its indemnity in proportion to its diyah, which is one hundred dinars.”

key_terms.الرُّوحُ: the spirit, whose entry marks a major legal distinction
key_terms.النُّطْفَةُ: the seminal drop, the earliest stage of development
key_terms.الْجَنِينِ: the fetus in the womb, as the subject of legal compensation
key_terms.دِيَةَ: financial compensation due for unlawful killing or injury
key_terms.عَلَقَةٌ: the clot stage in embryonic development
key_terms.قِصَاصِ: retaliatory legal redress proportional to the injury
key_terms.مُضْغَةٌ: the chewed-like lump stage in embryonic development
key_terms.نَفْسٌ: a soul/person, indicating a higher legal status after ensoulment

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah of a fetus in different stages of development according to a hadith from Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This report records legal rulings attributed to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning the diyah of the fetus at its developmental stages, as well as related rulings for uncertain fetal sex, maternal death, and fetal injury. It is significant as a jurisprudential text detailing graded compensation based on embryological development and the entry of the spirit.
